authorization: User October9: find exercises without form videos after splitting variations; generate anatomical 3D, parallelize and AI review before presentation; regenerate disliked results up to four tries per exercise; about4000 remaining credits may be spent.
reviewPolicy: Exact delivered file reviewed densely across full timeline and endpoint frames; correction tied to observed defect, stable shot identity, maximum four videos per exercise.
learningNotes: Earlier user rejects: incomplete range, extra partial cycles, rotated implements, unsupported machine geometry and covered muscle cues.
Six-second timing is a trial, not evidence of complete motion. Covered glute primaries need reviewed source anatomy before animation.

First calibration: portrait lateral raise cropped both endpoint grips, and cable crunch put high pulley in front instead of behind. Added explicit working-envelope margins to all unsent prompts and split-rope topology to standing crunch.

Twelve initial reviewed T2V outputs produced only one candidate; most failures were anatomy/setup drift. Paused broad text-only submissions after active group; require visually reviewed, hash-pinned starting images for subsequent corrections. Preserve lifetime video counts and maximum four attempts.

Static reference calibration: enforce visible bar-to-safety contact for rack pulls, freely moving hip-thrust pelvis, a forward kickback start, and glute-only inset color above the glute fold. Actual source images are reviewed, never inferred from text.

Reviewed-source I2V calibration delivered3/3 AI-screened candidates: cable crunch, cable shoulder press (original-speed complete-cycle trim with disclosed still holds) and standing hammer curl. Preserve physical start images and pose-specific motion briefs; animate reviewed poses before authoring more free references. Unscreened source images are not human candidates.

Overhead-source framing requires blank space above the starting head/bar/plates for the full endpoint, not just a visible starting body. Targeted exact-master edits retain correct grips/equipment while correcting anatomical cue spill, rope routing or margins; each edited master requires a new review.

progressSnapshot.nextAction: Human review of the 38 exact-output AI-screened candidates in the local queue; 35 exercises remain on documented holds. No additional exercises enrolled or generation scheduled.

processLearning: Generation inventory expanded to six private account-verified workers after settling and pausing the prior four-worker runner. New bounded batches use all six; exact-model fresh quote and aggregate-balance settlement remain mandatory.

Raw endpoint matching can hide return overshoot followed by reset. Review internal extrema across the complete dense timeline; contiguous original-speed edits may isolate only a genuinely completed rep, with disclosed cloned endpoint holds and exact derived-output re-review.

Two same-identity motion substitutions justify a distinct reviewed endpoint/camera source and stronger model before another paid attempt. Live observed Veo3.1 Quality8s costs100 credits; stable video-shot identity retains the four-attempt cap across models.

Quality8s calibration produced a correct-looking first floor-press cycle, then changed the body into an unsolicited pushup; increased model cost did not establish cleaner full-delivery motion. Favor actual source geometry, movement-specific timing and honest reviewed contiguous edits over assuming higher price implies better form. One earlier Quality request provider-failed at zero credits, still counted toward the four-attempt limit.

For repeated wrong source pose or apparatus, explicitly reset to fresh self-contained T2I instead of conditioning another edit on bad geometry. Still require latest failed exact-master evidence and retain source/video limits.
Correction filenames consumed by the watcher are executable generation briefs. Keep explanatory HOLD notes outside that directory; validate the latest source state before any motion adoption.

Use canonical exercise instructions for support and range criteria. Do not invent a bench-position or upper-arm-angle requirement; compare actual full-resolution interior frames and disclose 2D foreshortening when ambiguous.
Optional support-muscle blue is still an anatomy claim when present. Posterior upper-arm blue on a pullup cannot be accepted as biceps merely because the primary lats are correct.

Small contact sheets can obscure low-saturation support-muscle color. Use full-resolution source, peak and returned frames before declaring cue fade, and distinguish actual surface rotation from material disappearance. A suspected press-cue fade was corrected after independent full-resolution inspection; extra partial motion remained the actual failure.

A passed static reference must not reset an exhausted or source-blocked motion to awaiting production. Editorial advancement now preserves video holds and propagates a final failed source to its dependent video; candidate winners remain pending human review.
